turns.prompt_text: I have a macbook air as well as a mac mini, could I plug in an hdmi cable between the two to use my macbook air as a display/peripherals
turns.response_html:
Connectivity Constraints

The HDMI ports on both the MacBook Air and Mac Mini are designed strictly for Video Output. Connecting an HDMI cable directly between these two machines will not facilitate a display connection, as neither device features an HDMI Input port. Modern computer hardware typically requires a dedicated capture card or specialized controller to accept an incoming video signal via cable.

Viable Alternatives

To utilize the MacBook Air as a secondary display or to share peripherals, consider the following built-in macOS solutions:

  • AirPlay to Mac: On macOS Monterey or later, the Mac Mini can stream its desktop to the MacBook Air wirelessly. This is accessible via the Control Center under Screen Mirroring.
  • Screen Sharing: The native macOS Screen Sharing application (located in /Applications/Utilities) provides remote control of the Mac Mini desktop from the MacBook Air interface.
  • Universal Control: This feature allows a single keyboard and trackpad to operate both Macs seamlessly when placed side-by-side. This is configured within System Settings > Displays > Advanced.
  • Target Display Mode: This legacy feature is not compatible with Apple Silicon or any recent Intel-based Mac models.

Technical Hardware Workarounds

If a low-latency, hardware-level connection is necessary, specific equipment is required:

  1. USB Video Capture Card: Connecting the Mac Mini HDMI output to a USB capture card plugged into the MacBook Air allows the video feed to appear within a camera preview window or specialized software.
  2. Luna Display: This hardware dongle plugs into the Mac Mini and utilizes the local network or a Thunderbolt/USB cable to turn the MacBook Air into a functional second monitor with high performance.

Virtual Workspace Integration

The inclusion of a Meta Quest 3 significantly expands the "Mission Control" workspace capabilities. While physical HDMI connections remain restricted to output-only, the headset enables a high-fidelity virtual display environment through software conduits.

Primary Software Solutions

  • Immersed: This platform stands as a premier choice for productivity. It allows for the instantiation of up to five virtual monitors from a single Mac. High-resolution textures and low-latency streaming make this ideal for software engineering and complex system architecture.
  • Virtual Desktop: Known for its stability and performance, this application mirrors the Mac desktop into a variety of virtual environments. It is particularly effective for single-monitor focused deep work or high-bitrate media consumption.
  • Horizon Remote Desktop: Provided by Meta, this utility allows for a simple transition of the Mac Mini or MacBook Air screen into the Horizon environment, though it offers fewer customization options than Immersed.

High-Speed Connectivity Optimization

The presence of both high-speed Wi-Fi and wired Ethernet is optimal for spatial computing.

Network Strategies

  • Wired Stability: To achieve the lowest possible latency, a USB-C to Ethernet adapter can be connected to the Quest 3. Adapters utilizing the RTL8153 chipset are confirmed to be compatible with Horizon OS, providing a stable, high-bitrate connection that surpasses standard Wi-Fi performance.
  • Wireless Flexibility: A Wi-Fi 6 or 6E network provides sufficient bandwidth for wireless operation, allowing for movement within the "Mission Control" environment without cable tethering.
  • Peripheral Sharing: When using these virtual workspace apps, the keyboard and trackpad connected to the Mac Mini or MacBook Air function seamlessly within the virtual space.

The "Mission Control" Virtualization

The 10-monitor physical desk project can be supplemented or mirrored through virtual instantiation. This hybrid approach allows for:

  1. Context Isolation: Placing documentation and terminal windows on virtual side-monitors while maintaining the primary IDE on a physical display.
  2. Spatial Organization: Utilizing the Quest 3 to wrap virtual displays 360 degrees around the workstation.
  3. Digital/Physical Synergy: Utilizing "Passthrough" mode on the Quest 3 to maintain visual awareness of the physical Bambu Lab A1 printer or custom PCB prototypes while viewing virtual schematics.
